findings.title: Deferred-tx fee credits block_burn even when actor/owner cannot pay → unbacked mint
findings.reason: block_burn += deferred_fees.burn runs unconditionally after the debit attempt; with an underfunded actor and no owner entitlement, from_actor+from_owner < deferred_fee but full burn is still credited (no sender backstop on deferred path), breaking value conservation across validators.

findings.title: Swallowed store writes in deferred fee path leave half-updated state / credited burn
findings.reason: `let _ = store.set_actor(...)` and `let _ = checker.store_mut().set_account(...)` discard Err, yet block_burn is still credited and the entitlement was already consumed — a failed debit yields credited-but-uncollected fees.

findings.title: Actor-pays-for-gas has no caller authorization: any sender can drain a funded actor
findings.reason: Fee is debited from actor.balance for every ExecuteActor tx from any sender; attacker pays ~0 and can spam cheap calls to drain a victim actor's balance (and the granted owner's budget).

findings.title: consume_use_owner_balance charges full amount to entitlement budget before owner solvency is known
findings.reason: total_amount_used += amount and save_entitlement happen inside the checker, but the caller only debits from_owner = remainder.min(owner.balance); an underfunded owner still consumes the full remainder from max_total_amount budget.

findings.title: Main-path owner fallback: entitlement budget consumed for amount sender ends up paying
findings.reason: When owner_account.balance < remainder, owner_paid < remainder so sender covers the shortfall via sender_pays, but the entitlement's total_amount_used was already incremented by the full remainder, wasting/over-charging the grant budget.

findings.title: Deferred-tx path credits full burn regardless of amount actually debited — mints CBY into burn sink
findings.reason: `self.block_burn += deferred_fees.burn` adds the whole fee even when actor+owner balances cover less (from_actor+from_owner < deferred_fee), breaking supply conservation; this is exactly COW-2287/esc-20260616 which the merged code fixed via deferred_debit_split burning only `debited`.

findings.title: Actor balance uses non-existent Actor.balance field instead of canonical Account[actor].balance (Model A.5)
findings.reason: FundActor does `target_actor.balance += amount` and fee-deduction does `target_actor.balance -= from_actor`, but the `Actor` struct has no balance field (native balance lives in `Account`), so this either fails to compile or creates a shadow gas pot divorced from the transfer/token/query ledger users see.

findings.title: Any external sender can force a victim actor to pay its gas (fee-payer inversion, CIP-3 sender-pays relaxed with no CIP)
findings.reason: For ExecuteActor the actor balance is debited FIRST (from_actor = total_fee.min(balance)) before the signer, so an attacker can spam no-op handler calls to drain a funded actor's balance at ~zero cost, deviating from CIP-3's sender-pays model without any spec amendment authorizing it.

findings.title: UseOwnerBalance budget consumed for full requested amount even when owner pays less / nothing
findings.reason: consume_use_owner_balance increments total_amount_used and used_count by the full `remainder` before the caller balance-caps the real owner debit (from_owner = remainder.min(owner.balance)), so max_total_amount depletes faster than actual spend and the entitlement is consumed even when the owner has zero balance.

findings.title: PVM CBOR codec behavior change without activation/flag-day gate alters state root
findings.reason: Adding `type(value).__name__ == 'int'/'float'` makes values that previously fell through (deterministic TypeError) now encode, changing on-chain actor return serialization → receipts/state_root; a consensus-affecting encoding change that needs coordinated rollout, not an in-place edit.

findings.title: Scope::Actor overloaded to carry the paying owner address, contradicting its 'entitled actor' meaning
findings.reason: consume_use_owner_balance extracts the balance-paying owner from `Scope::Actor(addr)`, but Scope::Actor semantically denotes the actor whose resources are entitled; the CLI sets --scope-actor to the wallet/owner, repurposing the field away from its defined meaning.

findings.title: New wire variants minted in node-local codec, not the external cowboy-protocol codec (wire SoT)
findings.reason: FundActor=41 / Action::UseOwnerBalance=18 are reserved only in node's hand-rolled codec; the authoritative wire definition lives in the pinned external cowboy-protocol-codec crate, which this diff does not touch, so the opcodes must be independently mirrored there (they were, at 41/18) or any future migration to the re-exported codec silently remaps/collides these opcodes across repos.

findings.title: FundActor.amount (u64 wei) serialized as a raw JSON number by indexer
findings.reason: amount is emitted as a bare JSON number; values >= 2^53 wei lose precision in JS consumers (wallet/indexer clients), whereas sibling monetary event fields deliberately use *_u128_str string encoding to avoid exactly this — the new field perpetuates the precision-unsafe convention.

findings.title: Any sender can drain a funded actor's balance by forcing it to pay gas for attacker-initiated calls
findings.reason: ExecuteActor fee is debited from target_actor.balance first with sender_pays=total_fee-actor_paid, so any attacker sends cheap ExecuteActor txs to any funded actor, gets free execution (sender pays 0) and drains the victim actor's funds — no authorization that the caller may spend actor balance.

findings.title: UseOwnerBalance fallback lets an arbitrary caller drain the granting owner's account
findings.reason: consume_use_owner_balance debits the owner account for any sender who triggers the actor (owner only authorized the actor, not the caller), so attacker spam against the actor amplifies into a drain of the third-party owner's balance up to max_total_amount.

findings.title: Deferred-tx fee deduction swallows store errors on a consensus state-write path (fork risk)
findings.reason: `if let Ok(Some(mut target_actor))`, `let _ = set_account(...)` and `let _ = set_actor(...)` discard node-local store errors while mutating actor/owner balances and block_burn, so a transient error on one validator diverges state from others → latent multi-validator fork (same class as the fail-closed settlement gate).

findings.title: Deferred path over-credits block_burn vs actually collected fee (supply inflation)
findings.reason: block_burn += deferred_fees.burn (full) fires even when from_actor+from_owner < deferred_fee and there is no sender fallback, so when the actor/owner are underfunded the chain burns more than it collected, breaking value conservation / minting supply.

findings.title: Entitlement budget consumed by full remainder even when owner pays less
findings.reason: consume_use_owner_balance increments total_amount_used by `amount` before solvency is known; the caller then debits only remainder.min(balance), so the owner's granted budget is depleted faster than funds are actually spent.

findings.title: Full burn+tip credited while sender.balance.saturating_sub can under-debit (unbacked mint into burn/tip sink)
findings.reason: block_burn += fees.burn and block_tip += fees.proposer_tip are added unconditionally, but the actual debit is actor_paid(min)+owner_paid(min)+sender.balance.saturating_sub(sender_pays); in the actor-pays model the sender may be insolvent, so under-debit while burn/tip are minted in full breaks supply conservation (this is exactly what the later COW-966 escrow was added to prevent).

findings.title: Deferred-tx fee over-burns: block_burn += full deferred_fees.burn but actor/owner may cover only part with no sender fallback
findings.reason: from_actor = deferred_fee.min(actor.balance) and the owner remainder is dropped when the entitlement path returns None or the owner is insolvent (no sender fallback here), yet self.block_burn is incremented by the full deferred_fees.burn, minting unbacked value into the burn sink.

findings.title: consume_use_owner_balance charges full amount to entitlement budget before caller confirms owner can pay
findings.reason: total_amount_used/used_count are incremented by the full `amount`, but the caller only debits from_owner = amount.min(owner.balance); an insolvent owner still consumes the max_total_amount budget for value never transferred, over-consuming the entitlement and widening the burn-vs-debit shortfall.

findings.title: Deferred-fee settlement swallows set_account/set_actor errors, allowing burn without persisted debit
findings.reason: owner and actor balance writes use `let _ = ...set_account(...).await` / `let _ = store.set_actor(...)`, so a failed persist silently drops the debit while block_burn was already increased, breaking conservation and hiding store errors.

findings.title: Unconditional actor-pays fee attribution changes state_root for every existing ExecuteActor tx (flag-day fork)
findings.reason: Previously sender.balance -= total_fee; now the engine debits actor.balance (then owner) first for ALL ExecuteActor txs with no activation-height gate, so a node on the old binary and one on the new binary compute different post-block balances → state_root divergence on identical inputs = consensus fork the instant this deploys.

findings.title: Deferred-tx path now debits actor balance and adds to block_burn — new committed bytes vs old binary
findings.reason: Deferred txs previously paid no fee; the added block used to mutate target_actor.balance AND self.block_burn (which feeds burn/tip distribution and thus state), so existing deferred txs now yield a different state_root/burn accounting than the prior version → mixed-version fork with no gate.

findings.title: New SystemInstruction::FundActor (opcode 41) accepted by new nodes, InvalidEnum-rejected by old
findings.reason: A block containing a FundActor tx verifies on new binaries but the Read impl returns Error::InvalidEnum on old ones (same for Action::UseOwnerBalance opcode 18), so the block is valid on one partition and rejected on the other → requires coordinated flag-day activation, absent here.

findings.title: Non-deferred owner path unconditionally writes owner Account (via Account::new fallback) even when from_owner==0
findings.reason: When consume_use_owner_balance returns an owner whose account is absent, set_account materializes a fresh zero-balance account into state; deterministic but adds a state entry that the pre-patch binary never creates, compounding the state_root divergence and diverging from the guarded deferred path.
